plan.summary: Mature grower, predictable cash flows (light assets, low leverage) → DCF primary, comps cross-check.

methods.name: DCF (Standalone)
methods.reason: predictable, positive free cash flow makes cash flows the most direct measure

methods.name: Public Comps: Sector Peers
methods.reason: mature grower with low leverage: enterprise multiples compare cleanly

methods.name: DCF with Synergies
methods.reason: value to a buyer, synergies included: an offer price, not a standalone value

methods.name: Just Synergies
methods.reason: pre-announcement price plus the synergies: an offer price, not a standalone value

methods.name: LBO
methods.reason: what a financial buyer could pay given the cash flows and debt capacity

methods.name: Precedent Transactions
methods.reason: includes a control premium; not a standalone value

notes: Public Comps: Sector Peers has weight but didn't run; its weight was spread over the others

headlines.answer: CVS is worth about $103.19 a share (range $74.73–$152.95).
headlines.field: One weighted method so far: $74.73–$152.95 a share.
headlines.spread: 80% of 2,000 simulated runs land between $74.73 and $152.95.
headlines.sensitivity: Each 0.5-point change in the discount rate moves value about $8.04 a share; the grid spans $80.07–$149.88.
